en_normal.text: So the way I'm thinking about this is we should split the migration into three phases. First, we stand up the new database schema alongside the old one, without touching any of the existing red paths. Second, we backfill the historical data in batches, probably overnight, so we don't hammer production during business hours. Third, once we've verified the backfill is complete and the checksums match, we cut over the right path and start dual writing for a week before we retire the old table entirely. The biggest risk here is that backfill jobs silently dropping rows if the source table gets a schema change mid-migration, so I want someone watching the row counts the whole time, not just checking them at the end.

zira_clip.text: When I joined the team, the biggest challenge was that our on-call rotation had no documented escalation path, so every incident turned into a scramble to find whoever happened to be awake. I spent the first two weeks just interviewing engineers and writing down what they already knew informally. Then I put together a runbook that mapped each alert to a specific owner and a specific set of first steps, and we ran two tabletop exercises to stress test it before relying on it for real. Within a month our mean time to acknowledge dropped by more than half, and just as importantly, people stopped dreading their on-call weeks because they finally had something concrete to follow instead of guessing.
